mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 700K units signals increased consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence indices
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of instances when HOUST > 700K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals accommodative monetary policy, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in accommodative periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 8% signals improved labor market conditions, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, but only during late-cycle expansions.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 30% of late-cycle instances when UNRATE < 8%, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) growth exceeds 5% YoY and GDP (GDPC1) growth exceeds 3% YoY, the combined signal predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to robust economic activity.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO YoY growth > 5% and GDPC1 YoY growth > 3%
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 35% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.025 over any 2.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales (RSAFS) growth above 10% YoY signals strong consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, but this effect is muted during monetary tightening cycles.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 45% of non-tightening instances when RSAFS YoY growth > 10%, or Rank IC < 0.015 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always, the level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) inversely predicts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as higher rates discount future cash flows more heavily.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or the relationship between FEDFUNDS and 20-day forward SPX returns is not significantly inverse (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth exceeds 200K jobs per month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 9%, the combined signal predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to a strong labor market.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) declining by more than 2% YoY, coupled with a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 1%, signals a high likelihood of negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to supply chain disruptions and tight monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 55% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 2.5-year rolling window.
